headline: Russian drone kills a child in central Kyiv; Iran floats a seven-day Hormuz roadmap; France moves to guard Saudi’s Yanbu as Houthis escalate; Trump–Xi Day 2 heads to the Archives; Claude Opus 5.5 targets longer coding sessions.

stories.title: Russian drone hits Kyiv high-rise; 14-year-old killed
facts: Ukrainska Pravda / Kyiv police: Russian drone hit a 16-storey residential building in Pecherskyi (~9th–10th floors); a 14-year-old boy was killed and at least seven residents injured.
hromadske / Air Force: overnight–morning barrage of 295 drones (52 jet-powered); air defences shot down or suppressed 267 as of 07:30; strikes at 16 locations.
Capital damage: Solomianskyi non-residential hit + fire; Podilskyi six-storey non-residential fire; overnight debris injured one when it hit a 25-storey building in Solomianskyi.
Also: Zaporizhzhia — two hospitals damaged (five evacuated from one); Kyiv Oblast fires/damage in Boryspil, Brovary, Obukhiv districts.
stories.whyItMatters: Fresh civilian toll in the capital as Russia’s harder-to-intercept high-flying drones keep pressure on Kyiv and the south.

stories.title: Iran pitches seven-day roadmap to reopen Hormuz
facts: FM Abbas Araghchi (NY/UNGA sidelines, Thu): Tehran proposes a seven-day plan to implement the June MoU — halt hostilities and reopen the Strait of Hormuz.
NYT/Al Jazeera: end fighting all fronts (incl. Gaza/Lebanon) in 7 days; US release ≥$12bn assets, waive oil sanctions, lift blockade; Hormuz reopens day 7; nuclear talks start.
Passed via mediators earlier this week; unnamed White House official to CNN: “positive and constructive discussions”; NYT: Washington “would not rush into a deal.”
Analysts note the June 17 Pakistani/Qatari MoU’s 60-day window already collapsed — timetable is far more aggressive than anything that held.
stories.whyItMatters: A material diplomatic ask after morning’s Senate Iran war-powers vote — oil and Hormuz traffic still hinge on whether Washington bites.

image.alt: Iran pitches seven-day roadmap to end conflict with US

stories.title: France to guard Yanbu as Houthis escalate on Saudi
facts: Macron (TF1/France 2): France will send “soldiers, radars and defence systems” to protect Saudi Red Sea oil terminal Yanbu — “not to involve ourselves in any conflict, but to protect the site.”
Saudi-led coalition: intercepted six Houthi ballistic missiles Thu (alerts for Mecca, Yanbu, Taif, Jeddah, Tabuk); Houthis claimed Aramco Yanbu + a Riyadh “sensitive target.”
Saudi/Pakistan/Türkiye FMs set urgent chiefs-of-staff talks under Mecca Joint Defence Agreement (attack on one = attack on all) — pact not yet formally triggered.
Al Jazeera: Brent briefly topped $108 Thu (+3%), eased to ~$105.77 Fri morning; Houthis’ Mocha/island gains tighten Bab al-Mandab leverage as Hormuz stays constrained.
stories.whyItMatters: Allied hard power is shifting to Saudi export infrastructure while Yemen fighting and pipeline disruption keep oil elevated.

image.alt: Saudi Arabia allies line up support as Houthi attacks mount

stories.title: Trump–Xi Day 2: Taiwan line, warm dinner, Archives tour
facts: Material update vs morning (Xinhua/BBC): Xi urged US to “oppose Taiwan independence” and handle Taiwan “with prudence”; Washington has not publicly endorsed that wording.

State dinner Thu: warm toasts (Trump: “never gotten along better”; Xi: AI must stay “under human control”); tech CEOs at table (Cook, Huang, Musk, Altman, Pichai, Bezos, Zuckerberg) — Anthropic notably absent per BBC.
Substance still thin: $14bn Taiwan arms package remains paused as Trump’s “negotiating chip”; trade-truce extension already known from prior briefs.
Fri schedule (BBC): tea in the Red Room, then National Archives tour (Constitution / Declaration / Bill of Rights); Xi departs Washington later Friday.
stories.whyItMatters: Optics and a sharper Taiwan ask dominate Day 2 — still no public breakthrough on AI rules, tariffs, or arms sales.

stories.title: Claude Opus 5.5: priced for longer, context-heavy coding
facts: Anthropic Claude blog (Sep 24): Opus 5.5 estimated ~40% cheaper than Opus 5 for typical token-billed workloads — aimed at longer Claude Code sessions.
Usage trends Mar–Sep 2026: Claude works 3.3× longer per prompt, >40% more model calls/prompt, 68% fewer interruptions; context/request up 2.6×; input:output ratio 189:1 → 324:1.
Pricing: input/output −20%; cached-token reads −60% (cache reads dominate agentic bills). Output >30% faster than Opus 5.
Harness: harder to break cache mid-session; 1-hour cache lifetime for API/cloud; forked subagents inherit parent cache; effort level can change without cache reset on Opus 5.5 / Fable 5.1.
stories.whyItMatters: A major Anthropic product/pricing beat for agentic coding — primary source is the company post, not press rewrites.

facts.text: Bundestag (redo vote after July snafu): Bundespolizeigesetz passes with Kanzlermehrheit — 322 yes / 134 no / 118 abstain; adds TKÜ powers vs extremism/smuggling + sample weapons-zone checks.
heise/Wardle: Meta’s macOS Muse agent was ClickFix-hijackable for days via undocumented endo_voyager_dictation_endpoint; Meta removed the knob, still disputes “remote exploit” framing.
NASA Earth Observatory: Hurricane Polo underwent explosive intensification (Fri APOD companion: Omega Centauri).
HN top: Dutch DAWO community building a NixOS-based digitally autonomous government workplace as a Microsoft alternative (open building blocks for OS/cloud/collab/AI).
Cursor blog: improved token efficiency for longer agent runs (dev-tools note; not a full product launch).
Claude blog: Claude Tag now supports personal connectors in channels — smaller Marketplace/channels feature → notes, not a lead.
